Name: Requiring large private businesses to enable their customers to connect to a human customer service agent.
Title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to requiring large private businesses to enable their customers to connect to a human customer service agent
BodyName: Committee on Consumer and Worker Protection

History.Description: This Introduction was Introduced by Council
This Introduction was Referred to Comm by Council to the Committee on Consumer and Worker Protection

Summary: This bill would prohibit large private businesses from representing that customer service is available through a platform that it does not provide to customers and require disclosure to users that they are not interacting with a human customer service agent. In addition, the bill would require large private businesses to provide their New York City customers with the option to connect to a human customer service agent and to make a good faith effort to do so within 15 minutes or provide an appointment within one business day. Large private businesses would also be required to limit hold or wait times to 15 minutes at a time and cumulative hold or wait times or escalation queues to one hour in total. Violations would carry civil penalties of $5,000 for an initial violation and $10,000 for each subsequent violation.
Text:
A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to requiring large private businesses to enable their customers to connect to a human customer service agent

Be it enacted by the Council as follows:


Section 1. Chapter 5 of title 20 of the administrative code of the city of New York is amended by adding a new subchapter 27 to read as follows:
SUBCHAPTER 27
CUSTOMER SERVICE
§ 20-883 Definitions. For purposes of this subchapter, the following terms have the following meanings:
Artificial intelligence model. The term “artificial intelligence model” means an engineered or machine-based system that varies in its level of autonomy and that can, for explicit or implicit objectives, infer from the input it receives how to generate outputs that can influence physical or virtual environments.
Chatbot. The term “chatbot” means any artificial intelligence model that generates information via text, audio, image, or video in a manner that simulates interpersonal interactions or conversation. The term “chatbot” includes, but is not limited to, a chatbot used by an entity to provide: (i) direct customer service, including service to prospective and existing customers, relating to the sale or delivery of goods or services; or (ii) direct customer support, including technical assistance functions relating to the sale or delivery of goods or services.
Customer. The term “customer” means a natural person residing in the city who purchases, leases, or rents goods or services offered by or provided from a large private business. For purposes of this subchapter, residence refers to the customer’s account address.
Customer service. The term “customer service” means assistance by a large private business to a prospective or existing customer, in response to an inquiry from such customer, regarding a product, service, account, refund, billing matter, complaint, cancellation request, fraud claim, or dispute in relation to the sale or purchase of a good or service.
Customer service agent. The term “customer service agent” means a natural person who, as an employee, contractor, or representative of a large private business, provides either of the following: (i) direct customer service, including service to prospective and existing customers, relating to the sale and delivery of goods and services; or (ii) direct customer support, including technical assistance functions relating to the sale and delivery of goods and services.
Customer service platform. The term “customer service platform” means a means of communication made available to customers for the provision of the following: (i) direct customer service, including service to prospective and existing customers, relating to the sale and delivery of goods and services; or (ii) direct customer support, including technical assistance functions relating to the sale and delivery of goods and services.
Large private business. The term “large private business” means a business with more than $500,000,000 in gross annual revenue nationally that provides goods and services to customers.
Regular business hours. The term “regular business hours” means the hours during which a business usually makes customer service platforms available to customers, excluding days that the business is ordinarily closed and state and federal holidays. “Regular business hours” includes an 8-hour period per day.
Services. The term “services” means services for which a customer will provide or has provided monetary consideration, whether through a one-time payment, subscription, fee, or recurring charge. “Services” do not include services or parts of services that offer a free option to persons with an opportunity to pay, subscribe, or otherwise provide monetary consideration for the service or upgraded services at a future time.
Single-step transfer mechanism. The term “single-step transfer mechanism” means a clearly identified, accessible option consisting of a single step—including but not limited to a button, voice command, or menu selection—that, when activated by the customer: (i) initiates transfer to, or queuing for, a customer service agent; and (ii) does not require the customer to complete additional automated steps, answer additional questions, provide justification for the transfer request, or navigate additional menus or processes prior to transfer, unless such menu or process serves solely to route the customer to the appropriate customer service agent.
§ 20-884 Representations of customer service availability. a. A large private business shall not represent that customer service is available through a customer service platform, such as a telephonic or online chatbot customer service platform, if the merchant does not provide such a customer service platform.
b. For the purposes of this section, the listing of a large private business’s contact information does not constitute a representation that customer service is available through such a customer service platform unless it is accompanied by language indicating that customer service is available through such customer service platform, such as by using the term “customer service,” “contact us,” or similar language, to accompany that contact information.
§ 20-885 Disclosure requirements. a. A chatbot customer service platform provider shall provide clear, conspicuous, and explicit notice to users that such users are interacting with a chatbot rather than a human prior to the chatbot generating any outputs, every hour thereafter, and each time a user prompts the chatbot about whether it is a human. 
b. The notice shall be provided in the medium in which the chatbot interacts with the user and in the same language as the one in which the user is interacting with the chatbot. The notice shall be accessible to users with disabilities.
c. The text of any such notice provided pursuant to subdivision a of this section must appear in a font size similar to surrounding text and easily readable by an average user.
§ 20-886 Customer service agents. a. During at least a large private business’s regular business hours, a large private business shall provide customers with a single-step transfer mechanism on all platforms through which the large private business provides customer service, including online chatbot customer service and telephonic customer service platforms, that allows customers to request to connect to a customer service agent.
b. A large private business shall make a good faith effort to provide a customer who requests to connect to a customer service agent through the single-step transfer mechanism described in subdivision a of this section with one of the following:
1. Connection to a customer service agent within 15 minutes of the request; or
2. A specific appointment time within one business day of the request at which a customer service agent will call or connect with the customer.
c. A large private business shall make a good faith effort to ensure a customer is not placed on hold or made to wait for more than 15 minutes at any time after connection with a customer service agent, and that cumulative hold or wait times or escalation queues do not exceed one hour in total.
d. For purposes of subdivisions b and c of this section, the use of commercially reasonable and practicable standards that are designed and intended to achieve compliance shall satisfy the “good faith effort” requirements.
e. A large private business that provides goods and services to customers in the city through an online platform and that has a telephonic customer service platform shall post its telephonic customer service telephone number clearly and conspicuously on its website.
f. This section does not require a large private business to do any of the following:
1. To connect or respond within 15 minutes if the request or connection is made via electronic mail, web-based contact form, or voicemail message;
2. To offer customer service through a communication platform that the business has not otherwise made available to customers as of the effective date of the local law that added this subchapter; or
3. To provide telephonic customer service if the large private business did not utilize any telephonic customer service platform as of the effective date of the local law that added this subchapter, provided that the large private business offers customer service methods by which a customer may promptly connect with a customer service agent consistent with this section.
g. A large private business’s inability to comply with this section does not constitute a violation of this section if that inability is due to either of the following:
1. Unforeseen circumstances beyond its reasonable control; or
2. An extraordinary or emergency situation, including a grid emergency or public safety power shutoff event, or an information technology or telecommunications outage.
§ 20-887 Rules. The department, or any other agency or office designated by the mayor, shall promulgate rules in furtherance of the implementation and enforcement of this subchapter.
§ 20-888 Penalties. Any person who violates any provision of this subchapter or any rule promulgated thereunder shall be subject to a civil penalty of not more than $5,000 for an initial violation and $10,000 for each subsequent violation.
§ 20-889 Enforcement by the corporation counsel. The corporation counsel or such other persons designated by the corporation counsel on behalf of the department may initiate in any court of competent jurisdiction any action or proceeding that may be appropriate or necessary for correction of any violation issued pursuant to this subchapter, including mandating compliance with the provisions of this subchapter or such other relief as may be appropriate.
§ 2. This local law takes effect 180 days after it becomes law.
